newsitem.title: FRANCE: No decision yet on use of France Telecom funds.
newsitem.headline: No decision yet on use of France Telecom funds.

text.p: The French government has not yet decided how to allocate funds due to be transferred from France Telecom next year in return for the state assuming the company's pension liabilities ahead of its partial privatisation, a finance ministry source said on Tuesday.

She said however that the government believed the funds could in theory be considered as a state revenue in determining the size of the budget deficit under the terms of the Maastricht treaty on monetary union.
French financial daily La Tribune Desfosses said on Tuesday that the France Telecom funds could help to reduce the budget deficit next year to three percent of gross domestic product.
It said the government had fixed the amount to be transferred to the state at 37.5 billion francs.
Bu the finance ministry source said the exact amount, due to be fixed in the 1997 budget which will be presented later this month, had not yet been decided.

Telecommunications Minister Francois Fillon said in June the state would charge France Telecom under 40 billion francs to assume the pension liabilities after January 1, 1997 when the state service will be changed into a limited company ahead of a partial privatisation.

Finance Minister Jean Arthuis indicated in May that the France Telecom funds would not be used to finance current budget spending, telling parliament the government would not confuse current and capital revenues.
The finance ministry source said that this remained the case and that the government was determined to produce a "clean" transparent budget.
Finance ministry sources have said previously that the France Telecom funds could be put into a separate account and used to meet the pension liabilities in the future.
The funds could nonetheless be counted as state revenues for the year when it comes to calculating the budget deficit.

Under the Maastricht treaty, revenues raised through privatisations must be excluded from the calculation of the size of the budget deficit. It however makes no provision for how to treat funds transferred to cover pension liabilities.
The government aims to reduce the budget deficit to three percent of GDP next year from a targetted four percent this year and five percent last year.
